newsitem.title: UK: UK signals readiness to lower gay sex age limit.
newsitem.headline: UK signals readiness to lower gay sex age limit.

text.p: Britain on Monday moved towards lowering the age of consent for homosexuals to 16 after the newly-elected Labour government said it would not contest a case before the European Court of Human Rights.
The British parliament voted three years ago to lower the age at which gays and lesbians can legally have sex to 18 from 21 but failed to bring the law into line with that of heterosexuals.

The decision prompted Euan Sutherland, a London homosexual who said he had a gay relationship at the age of 16, to challenge the law in the European Court, claiming that the ruling was discriminatory and breached his rights to privacy.

A government spokesman said on Monday that Prime Minister Tony Blair's government, elected on May 1, was unwilling to use large sums of public money to contest the case and was ready to settle out of court.

He said it would then be up to members of parliament to move towards another vote on the issue. An estimated two to one majority of MPs is now thought to support lowering the age limit following the landslide victory of the first Labour government for 18 years.
Gay rights campaigners welcomed the move, which follows the appointment by Blair of Chris Smith as the first openly homosexual British cabinet minister.

"We were always very hopeful that a new Labour government would concede the principle of equality and it looks as if this is going to happen," said Angela Mason, spokeswoman for the pressure group Stonewall.
